analytical_question: How far have generative AI and the specified support application diffused, what shapes that diffusion, and what timing implication follows for this organization?
general_et_finding: Aggressive posture makes generative AI late majority.
application_finding: The Information sector rate proves early-majority generative AI support diffusion.
organization_specific_finding: The hypothetical firm behaves as a fast follower, provisionally analogous to early-majority preferences for demonstrated usefulness. Its actual adopter category relative to peers is unknown because adoption dates and matched-peer data are absent. Human review and a knowledge base make structured learning plausible now, while limited engineering and evaluation capacity constrain pace. This posture changes the evidence threshold and timing, not the technology stage. Candidate change agents are the support manager and integration engineer; respected experienced support representatives could be opinion leaders, but their influence has not been observed. Software tooling and reusable guidance can ease experimentation; reliable documentation, access controls and evaluation skills are complementary assets. These mechanisms are hypotheses from the case. NIST guidance (S5) can structure shared expectations; no standard here proves readiness or market uptake.

evidence.claim: Rogers provides adopter categories and the five perceived attributes, not a fixed maturity score.
evidence.source_or_reference: S1 Rogers (2003), fifth edition; publisher author excerpt: https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Diffusion-of-Innovations-5th-Edition/Everett-M-Rogers/9780743222099
evidence.evidence_type: Original theoretical framework via publisher excerpt
evidence.notes: Five attributes cross-checked against publisher excerpt of fourth edition; framework does not supply current AI stage.

evidence.claim: US employed-adult generative AI work use was 40.54550% in Q3 2026, down from 45.19932% in Q2.
evidence.source_or_reference: S2 Bick, Blandin and Deming, RPS via FRED: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RPSGENAIUSAGESHAREWORK
evidence.evidence_type: Original survey series disseminated by FRED
evidence.notes: US employed adults 18–64, quarterly self-report, not seasonally adjusted; neither firms nor application penetration.

evidence.claim: May Census AI rates are broad AI context, not a support-specific denominator.
evidence.notes: 32% for 100–249 employees and 39.7% for Information are separate groups. Any AI in any business function. Newer October downloads not analyzed.

evidence.claim: One support-assistant deployment reported higher issues resolved per hour.
evidence.source_or_reference: S4 Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond (2023), Generative AI at Work: https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161 ; https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/working-papers/generative-ai-work
evidence.evidence_type: Original research abstract in search index
evidence.notes: 5,179 agents; 14% mean improvement in that version. Direct pages returned 403. No prevalence, autonomous safety or local ROI inference.

evidence.claim: NIST offers voluntary generative AI risk guidance.
evidence.source_or_reference: S5 Autio et al. (2024), NIST AI 600-1: https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1
evidence.notes: Governance resource, not certification or evidence of adoption.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No matched-peer, support-specific, current production-use denominator or longitudinal adoption dates were found.
Worker-use rates cannot establish firm rollout or autonomous support penetration. The latest quarterly worker estimate decreased.
S3 measures broader AI and is older than available October releases. Separate sector and size rates cannot be combined into a joint peer rate.
S4 is one older assisted-work deployment; indexed abstract verification is limited and does not establish diffusion or autonomous reliability.
All company details and change-agent roles are hypothetical. No interviews or actual operational measurements were performed.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence that general workplace use extends beyond pioneers; low confidence in a precise Rogers stage and no defensible measured category for the target peer group. Moderate confidence in the direction of the five application mechanisms; low confidence in local effect sizes. Timing advice is conditional on assumed capabilities.
value_opportunity_implication: Observed assistant benefits justify investigating whether drafting time and novice learning improve locally. Do not promise the study average or treat it as an ROI estimate.
risk_governance_implication: Knowledge quality, privacy and review capacity are the principal inferred inhibitors. Human send authority makes errors more containable but does not remove them. Apply appropriate evaluation and governance guidance (S5); the Adoption Agent must judge implementation feasibility and acceptable risk.
recommendation_management_implication: For the next six months, begin evidence gathering now: establish a baseline and use de-identified historical tickets for an offline drafting assessment during the first month. If evaluation capacity and confidentiality controls are demonstrated, ask the Adoption Agent to assess a small human-reviewed trial during months two and three. Review the evidence at month three before considering expansion; reserve months four to six for evidence-led learning. Diffusion does not itself justify rollout.
change_monitoring_triggers: Monthly: refresh the RPS/FRED series and examine direction without asserting statistical significance from point estimates alone.
Within one month: obtain recent matched-peer evidence reporting denominator, production versus pilot status, human review, firm size and geography.

Before a live trial: establish representative baseline metrics for time per ticket, audited correctness, reopen rate and customer satisfaction; require baseline-equivalent quality and lower total handling time including review. These are proposed criteria, not observed results.

At month three: reassess if documentation quality, evaluation staffing or data-handling controls remain inadequate; return to offline work if a material privacy event or customer-harming error appears.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Abstain on the claim that most comparable software firms use generative AI support drafting, or that this application is early majority. Require a recent representative survey of US B2B software firms with 100–249 employees, a stated sample and denominator, uncertainty estimates and separate pilot/production and assisted/autonomous measures.
Do not classify the focal firm as ahead of or behind peers without verified peer adoption dates and comparable use definitions.
Do not infer autonomous diffusion, safety or a full adoption recommendation from assisted-work evidence.
